                      STATUTES


                                           Life With Artificials


1      Name
1.1     The name of the association is Life With Artificials.


2      Purpose
2.1     The Association's purpose is to focus on and place "The 18. Sustainable Development Goal - Life with Artificials" on the national-
          le and global agenda as well as to create debates around potentials, dilemmas and risks in the use and development
       the generation of new technologies. This is achieved through the intersection of technology and art with the aim to provoke,
        create awareness and educate about the advantages and disadvantages for humanity and our planet in
       the use of new technology such as AI, ML, CRISPR and data collection. The focus is on the integration of "Artificials" in com-
The         fundet   must   occur    safely,   ethically   and   sustainably    for the   benefit⟧   of   humanity   and   the planet.

        The association investigates three doctrines: Mind the Future: A new era is coming, the epoch of humanized technology.
       Mine the Future: What does the future look like? If we don't like what we see, let us change the future in the present.
       Mind  the  Gap:  Mind the  distance between humans and   technologies. Between   present   and   future.


        The association's activities take place, among others, in collaboration and network with artists, relevant stakeholders, private
         companies, public authorities, educational institutions, foundations, associations, NGOs, and so forth. 2.2     The association may seek and distribute financial resources with a view to supporting the association's purpose.

3       Use of funds3.1     The board decides on the use of funds in accordance with the association's purpose.                                                                                                  Document key:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Penneo3.2     The board also decides on any transfer of the year's result to the association's equity.

4      Membership

4.1    Both natural and legal persons may become members of the association, whether domiciled in Denmark or
                 abroad, who can subscribe to the association's purpose.


4.2     Admission takes place by written application to the association stating name, address, email and telephone
        number.


4.3    Members pay a subscription fee, which is set for 1 years at a time at the association's ordinary general
         meeting after recommendation from the board.


4.4    Members of the association have the opportunity to participate   in various activities, for which the board sets
          guidelines.

4.6     The association's members are not liable for the association's obligations.


4.7     The Board may exclude a member if that membership, at the Board's discretion, is not

       member does not pay the fee mentioned under item 4.3. An excluded member may demand that the board

       reverse the association's decision on exclusion with a 2/3 majority.

5       General Meeting

5.1     Within the limits set by the legislation and these articles of association, the general assembly has the highest authority in all matters of the association.
        


5.2    Unless the members decide otherwise, the board calls for one annual ordinary general meeting on
         Zealand. Notice of the ordinary general meeting is sent by letter or e-mail to the members no later than two
          (2) weeks and at the earliest four (4) weeks before the general meeting. The ordinary general meeting shall be held each
         year no later than five (5) months after the end of the preceding financial year. 5.3     The agenda for the ordinary general meeting shall address the following points:

        •  Election of chairman for the general meeting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          document key:
        •  Chairman’s report on the association’s activities during the preceding financial year.
        •  Report on and approval of the association’s annual report for the preceding financial year, and decision on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Penneo
           membership fee.
        •  Possible proposals from the board and association members.
        •  Election of chairman and board
        •  Election of auditor(s).
        •  Any other business.


5.4     The board shall convene an extraordinary general meeting when a board member or a member of
        the association requests it. A request from a board member or a member of the association for the
        holding of an extraordinary general meeting must be accompanied by the agenda for the general meeting. Notice
        of an extraordinary general meeting shall be sent by letter or e-mail to the members as soon as possible after
        receipt of the request, to be held within fourteen (14) days and no earlier than eight (8) days from the notice
         . An extraordinary general meeting can also be convened by a member of the association.


5.5      Proposals to be presented at the ordinary general meeting must be submitted to the board no later than 1
       week(s) before the holding of the ordinary general meeting.

                                                                                              2

[Source page 3]

5.6     Notice of the general meeting shall be accompanied by the agenda for the general meeting and the complete
          proposals that will be presented at the general meeting, and, for the ordinary general meeting,
       also the annual report.


5.7     Every member of the association, the board, as well as the association's auditor, is entitled to participate at the general meeting
        .


5.8     The general assembly is quorate when at least half of the members are present or repre-
         center by proxy and participant in the voting.


5.9     Each member of the association has one vote at the general meeting.


5.10   Voting rights at the general meeting may be exercised by proxy. The proxy must bring the proxy document to the
        general meeting, but does not need to be a member of the association themselves.


5.11    No decisions can be made at the general meeting about proposals not included on the agenda,
       unless all members give their consent.

          check if it was passed at the general meeting and send this protocol note by letter or e-mail to the member-
       merne.


5.15    The association's general meetings are not open to the public.


5.16    Changes to these articles can only be adopted when at least 2/3 of the attendees and the members represented by proxy vote in favor. In addition, the changes must be registered with the Erhvervsstyrelsen if necessary.
        
         

6       Bestyrelsen

6.1     The board is responsible for the overall management of the association.

                                                                                              3

[Source page 4]

6.2     The board consists of 3-6 members, who are elected by the general meeting, cf. however point 6.4. The general meetin-
       g also elects the chairman of the board.


6.3     The board members are elected for 2 years at a time and may be re-elected.

6.4      The founder of the association, MindFuture ApS, cvr no. 41275677, has at any time the right—but not the obligation—to appoint
         a majority of the members of the board as well as the chairman of the board.


6.5     Minutes shall be kept of the board's negotiations, which shall be signed by all members present
        and sent to all members. A board member, a director, or an auditor who
         disagrees with the board's decision has the right to have their views recorded in the minutes.


6.6     The board may establish detailed provisions regarding the performance of its duties in rules of procedure.


6.7     The board keeps a register of the association's members.

7       Drawing rule

7.1     The association is signed by the chairman of the board together with a board member or by the entire board.

9      Resolution

9.1     The association can only be dissolved when at least 3/4 of the members of the board or at least 2/3 of the association's 
       members at a general meeting propose this. Such a proposal, however, must to be 
        considered be in the hands of the board    no later than six (6) weeks before the general meeting, so that the association's 
       members are made aware of it no later than two (2) weeks before the general meeting.


9.2      The proposal can only be adopted when at least 3/4 of all members present and represented by proxy
       of the association at two (2) consecutive general meetings, held with at least one
          (1) and at most two (2) months interval, vote in favour.


9.3     The association's assets are used, after all obligations have been met, to promote the purposes listed in item 2
         according to the general assembly's detailed decision.
